stops.name: Camp Nou
stops.en: If you're a football fanatic, then you can't miss a visit to this football temple, the home ground for Barcelona's biggest and most popular team and one of Europe's greatest footballing 'cathedrals'. During the Franco era, FCB was the only way that oppressed Catalans could vent their anger against his dictatorship. Because of that, it became and still is a symbol of Catalan identity. Camp Nou is t
stops.lc: El estadio de fútbol de Barcelona es el hogar del FC Barcelona. El lugar se inauguró en 1957 después de que el anterior estadio de fútbol, Camp de Les Corts, se considerara muy pequeño. El Camp Nou se ha convertido en una de las atracciones más visitadas de Barcelona. Tiene capacidad para 99.354 espectadores. En los terrenos del estadio hay una tienda de recuerdos, mini campos que se utilizan para

stops.name: Casa Milà
stops.en: One of Gaudi's masterpieces, there is not one straight edge on the exterior and the structure is one of Gaudi’s most eccentric and enticing architectural creations. Tours of the interior and the incredible roof structures are available. Great views of the tall buildings (especially La Sagrada Familia) from the roof. Hosts a large exposition of Gaudi works, covering Sagrada Familia and Casa Batlio,
stops.lc: El edificio de apartamentos fue construido entre 1906 y 1912 y hoy es Patrimonio de la Humanidad por la UNESCO albergando un centro cultural. Pedro Mila I Camps encargó a Gaudí el diseño del edificio. La estructura no tiene líneas rectas ni muros de carga, sino que se basa en pilares y soportes de acero. El diseño irregular incluye techos de diferentes alturas. Hay dos patios que permiten que todo

stops.name: Casa Batlló
stops.en: Another Gaudi masterpiece along the same avenue as La Pedrera. Open to the public. No straight line or right angles appear anywhere in the house. Often overlooked for La Pedrera, (also by Gaudi), La Casa Batlló is equally as stunning with its unique architecture and infamous two ornamental pillars in the entrance to the terrace. Open for visitors from ground floor to the roof, and down by an old-t
stops.lc: Casa Batlló es uno de los tres inusuales edificios que forman la "Manzana de la Discordia". En 1904 Gaudí recibió el encargo de reformar el edificio sustituyendo la fachada original por una obra en vidrio y piedra. El muro de la fachada se hizo curvar y doblarse como una ola, luego se enyesó y se cubrió con un mosaico de fragmentos de vidrio y cerámica de colores. La parte superior del edificio pa

stops.name: Torre Glòries
stops.en: Formerly known as Torre Agbar. Distinctively-shaped office tower which stands out in the Barcelona skyline. It stands out even more Friday, Saturday and Sunday nights when it is lighted in several colours. The viewing platform on the 30th floor has views in all directions. Tickets start at €15 and come with a complimentary glass of cava and access to Hyperview Barcelona, an exhibit of the city’s r
stops.lc: La Torre Glòries fue diseñada por el arquitecto francés Jean Nouvel y la construcción se completó en 2005. La torre tiene 38 plantas y su controvertida forma se asemeja a una bala. La forma se inspiró en un géiser que brotaba del suelo en la montaña de Montserrat, cerca de Barcelona. La forma se asemeja a la del "Gherkin" en Londres aunque también se inspiró en el campanario de la Sagrada Familia

stops.name: La Rambla
stops.en: Often the first landmark that people identify with the city. It is the central and most famous boulevard cutting through the heart of the city centre — a vibrant promenade filled with Barcelona life at its best. It stretches from the harbour to La Plaça Catalunya, running through the Ciutat Vella like a spine. Come here to see street performers, enjoy the flower and pet stalls, or just sit back an
stops.lc: La Rambla es un bulevar de 1,2 kilómetros de largo en el centro de Barcelona. La sección central del bulevar es solo para peatones. A lo largo del recorrido que va desde la fuente de Canaletes hasta el Monumento a Colón hay muchos edificios históricos. El bulevar se dispuso en 1766 y los edificios antiguos se demolieron, sin embargo, cada una de sus 5 secciones recibió el nombre de los edificios q

stops.name: Casa Vicens
stops.en: The first building Gaudi built in Barcelona. It has been opened as a museum. It's possible to walk the whole monumental enclosure, including the garden and the interior of the building. In UNESCO World Heritage Sites list since 2005.
stops.lc: Esta vivienda es una de las creaciones de Antoni Gaudí y fue construida entre 1883 y 1889 tras recibir el encargo de Manuel Vicens. El edificio tiene 4 plantas y su diseño está influenciado por el estilo oriental, indio, asiático y morisco. El exterior presenta azulejos verdes y blancos. Las ventanas de la fachada están arqueadas con delicados balcones y hay un efecto de tablero de ajedrez creado

stops.name: Casa Lleó Morera
stops.en: By Lluís Domènech i Montaner.
stops.lc: Este es uno de los tres edificios que componen la Manzana de la Discordia en el Passeig de Gracia. Destaca por su singular arquitectura creada por Lluis Domenech i Montaner, quien recibió el encargo en 1902 de remodelar el edificio construido en 1864. El arquitecto trabajó junto con destacados artesanos para la realización de las esculturas, vidrieras, la cerámica, la decoración interior y el dise

stops.name: Tàpies Museum
stops.en: Created in 1984 by the artist Antoni Tàpies to promote the study and knowledge of modern and contemporary art.
stops.lc: La Fundación Antoni Tapies es un centro cultural y museo creado por el artista catalán Antoni Tapies en 1984. Antoni Tapies creó la fundación para promover el arte moderno, aunque hoy en día se pueden ver obras de varios períodos históricos expuestas en el museo. El núcleo de la colección permanente provino de la donación original de Tapies de su colección personal. La mayoría de las obras expuest

stops.name: Basilica and Expiatory Church of the Holy Family
stops.en: Barcelona's most popular and famous attraction, the Sagrada Família is a testament to Antonio Gaudi's modernist style and unlike any other church in the world. The texture and detail on the façades are intricate and incorporate forms seen in nature as much of Gaudi's work does. The inside is huge — it's estimated that it can hold 13,000 people — with vaulted ceilings and columns designed to be rem

stops.name: Park Güell
stops.en: A large urban park heavily influenced by Antonio Gaudi. The area was originally meant to be a residential property development with Gaudi doing much of the planning and landscape design. Only two houses were built and the land was later sold to the city of Barcelona and turned into a park. There are two areas -- a relatively undeveloped (and un-crowded) natural area near the top of the hill and th

stops.name: Palau de la Música Catalana
stops.en: Modernist design by Lluís Domènech i Montaner is a UNESCO World Heritage site, a masterpiece of Catalan's modernist architecture. This auditorium designed by Ramon Muntaner is the most important Modernist example in Ciutat Vella. It was the headquarters of the Orfeó Català, the oldest Catalan choir. The most beautiful part is the stalls with its fine detailing, although all the build

stops.name: Cathedral of the Holy Cross and Saint Eulalia
stops.en: The main Gothic church in Barcelona. The cloister is maybe the most interesting part.

stops.name: Lluís Companys Olympic Stadium
stops.en: The stadium and its surroundings built in 1927 and renovated for the 1992 Summer Olympics provides nice architectonic and city views. Since it's not too crowded outside sport events, it's usually a pretty calm place.

stops.name: Hospital de Sant Pau
stops.en: This former hospital is an architectural masterpiece that is now open for visitors. Inpatient wards (and most outpatient facilities) have been moved to a new building of Nou Hospital, but in terms of touring the area, that makes it all the easier. One of "small hidden features" is a network of underground passages where small carriages can be seen, you can get there near WCs on a central square, b

stops.name: Palau Güell
stops.en: Palace designed by Gaudí for the industrial tycoon Eusebi Güell. There is a basement and three levels of the palace to explore, the highest featuring a small exhibition. It is in a different style to Gaudí's apartment blocks La Pedrera and Casa Batlló, as well as being cheaper and less crowded than those sites. The rooftop of Palau Güell features the more standard Gaudi style chimneys, and views a

stops.name: Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya
stops.en: Has the single best collection of Romanesque art in the world, and a fine Gothic collection as well. Includes the Pantocrator from the Taüll Romanesque church. The building itself is also very beautiful.

stops.name: Fundació Joan Miró
stops.en: Treasured museum dedicated to Joan Miró and always has interesting temporary expositions on display.
stops.lc: La Fundación Joan Miró es un museo dedicado a la obra de Joan Miró, catalán nacido en Barcelona. La fundación fue creada por Miro y Joan Prats en 1975. Su propósito era crear un lugar donde los jóvenes artistas pudieran experimentar con el arte contemporáneo y también tener un lugar para mostrar su trabajo. El diseño del espacio a través del edificio tiene un flujo natural junto con patios, terraz

stops.name: Basilica of Our Lady of the Sea
stops.en: One of the most representative examples of Catalan Gothic architecture, it features a sombre but beautiful interior. The upsweeping verticality and lightness of the interior are especially surprising considering the blocky exterior surfaces. Built between 1329 and 1383, it was once was home to a Christian cult in the late 3rd century. The church is dedicated to Saint Mary of the Sea, since the qua

stops.name: German Pavilion, Barcelona
stops.en: The Pavilion is one of the emblematic works of Mies van der Rohe and key reference architecture of the twentieth century. The famous German Pavilion was designed for the 1929 Barcelona International Exhibition and reconstructed in 1986 on its original site. Its innovative architectural structure marked a radical change in the layout of space and greatly influenced the development of modern archite

stops.name: MACBA Barcelona Museum of Contemporary Art
stops.en: Art from the second half of the twentieth century to today. Smart-phone app with free audio guides.

stops.name: La Boqueria
stops.lc: El Mercat de Sant Josep de la Boqueria es un enorme mercado a la entrada de La Rambla. La primera piedra del edificio del colocó en 1840 y se comenzó a construir según el proyecto del arquitecto Mas Vila. En 1871 se añadió al mercado el alumbrado de gas y en 1914 se inauguró el techo de metal. Muchos de los propietarios de puestos son comerciantes de tercera e incluso cuarta generación. El mercado

stops.name: Parc de la Ciutadella
stops.en: Barcelona's most central park, and includes a zoo, a lake and several museums. In fact, the park is so large, 74 acres, that the Catalan Parliament can be found in the centre of the park. It is a great place to enjoy games, sports or to spend a leisurely afternoon. It was built at the final part of the 19th century in the place that formerly occupied the fortress (ciutadella) built after the defea

stops.name: Torre de Collserola
stops.lc: La torre se construyó en 1991 como parte de una mejora de infraestructura para preparar la ciudad para los Juegos Olímpicos de 1992. El famoso arquitecto inglés Norman Foster diseñó una torre de aspecto Hi-Tech con una silueta poco convencional. La torre consta de una base de dos pisos cubierta de tierra con un fuste de hormigón de 205 metros de largo (4,5 metros de diámetro) y una sección de celo

stops.name: Aquarium Barcelona
stops.en: The second biggest aquarium in Europe. Watch thousands of fish, penguins and sharks in this interactive sea-life museum. Unlike Genoese Aquarium it has a long glass tube, where you can walk watching sharks and other fish swimming around.
stops.lc: El acuario de Barcelona cuenta con 35 tanques que albergan unos 11.000 peces y animales acuáticos de 450 especies. El acuario tiene el Oceanario con peces luna, rayas, tiburones y doradas, entre otros. Hay un túnel transparente de 80 metros de largo que lo atraviesa donde los visitantes pueden ver a los peces nadando a su alrededor mientras caminan por el túnel. Hay una serie de tanques temáticos

stops.name: Casa Amatller
stops.en: Designed by Puig i Cadafalch, the building is a fine work of Modernism. Check the detailed photos and explanation of facade sculptures. It also has a shop that sells fine chocolate (the Amatller family made its money out of cocoa).

stops.name: Poble Espanyol
stops.en: A fake village built in 1929, with replicas of characteristic buildings in Spain (like the Avila walls, the Vall-de-roures town hall, etc.). The village hosts the Fondation Fran Daurel, where you can enjoy an interesting Modern Art collection boasting Miró, Picasso, Tapiès and other, mostly Spanish and Catalan, contemporary artists. The audio tour is very worthwhile there. Also worth seeing - the

stops.name: Montjuïc Castle
stops.en: Provides a beautiful panorama view over the rest of the city. The Montjuic Castle is in the Montjuic hill. From the Montjuïc Castle, take the harbor cable car to Barceloneta for more splendid views.

stops.name: Maritime Museum of Barcelona
stops.en: Housed in Drassanes, the Gothic shipyard of the city. During the 14th century, the Aragó Crown was the most important power in the Mediterranean Sea, and this was the main place where the ships were built. Nowadays, it's the Maritime Museum, worth a visit for the architectonic structure, a still-standing part of the ancient medieval city wall (including a gate), and the reproduction of the

stops.name: Monastery of Pedralbes
stops.en: A beautiful Gothic monastery near the university, there are a museum which depicts the monastery life, a church, and a marvelous chapel covered with medieval frescoes.

stops.name: Plaça Sant Jaume
stops.en: This square has been the political hub since the Roman era. It has been witness to some of the most important events in modern Catalan history, such as the proclamation of the Catalan State in 1931. At one end, there is the Palace of the Generalitat (the one with two flags on the top, the government of the Autonomous Community of Catalunya) and on the other stands the City Hall (three flags). Both

stops.name: Gaudi House Museum
stops.en: Distinctive pink house that Gaudi lived in for nearly 20 years (although not designed by him). It features furniture designed by Gaudi and other objects relating to Gaudi's life. The gift shop has a large selection of Gaudi-themed souvenirs that are generally better quality than what's available in the normal tourist shops.

stops.name: Güell Pavilions
stops.en: A complex of two pavilions by Antonio Gaudi. 2024 closed for renovation.

stops.name: Hash Marihuana & Hemp Museum
stops.en: This museum in the modernist Palau Mornau offers a unique permanent exhibition on the development of the cannabis plant as a versatile source for industrial, nutritional, medicinal, sacramental and recreational purposes.

stops.name: Jardí Botànic de Barcelona
stops.en: Although a botanic garden had been established in Barcelona as early as 1888, the current gardens date from 1999.

stops.name: Old Hospital de la Santa Creu, Barcelona
stops.en: This Gothic building was the old city hospital, before the modernist Hospital de Sant Pau was built in l'Eixample. Now the hospital has the National Library inside, and is a great example of civilian Gothic archictecture.

stops.name: Sant Pau del Camp
stops.local: Monasterio de San Pablo del Campo
stops.en: A rare example of Romanesque architecture, the prettiest in Barcelona. Its name reflects the fact that the church was once surrounded by green fields outside the city walls.

stops.name: Centre de Cultura Contemporània de Barcelona
stops.local: Centro de Cultura Contemporánea de Barcelona
stops.en: The arts centre’s core theme is the city and urban culture.
stops.lc: El CCCB es una de las galerías de arte y espacios expositivos más populares de Barcelona. Está enfocado en la vida de la ciudad contemporánea y la cultura urbana de Barcelona. El centro alberga exposiciones, conferencias, clases, recitales de danza, debates, eventos audiovisuales, proyecciones de películas, festivales y más. Sirven de nexo entre el mundo académico, los artistas y el público en gen

stops.name: Natural Science Museum of Barcelona
stops.local: Museo de Ciencias Naturales de Barcelona
stops.en: Museum with a number of exhibitions about the Earth and its natural history. One exhibit covers the origin of life on Earth and how it has evolved. A second exhibit deals with nature and life on Earth today. The third exhibit covers some of the issues relating to humans and their relationship with nature.
stops.lc: El Museu de Ciències Naturals de Barcelona es una institución con más de tres millones de ejemplares en los ámbitos de la mineralogía, la petrología, la paleontología, la zoología y la botánica. Está situado desde 2011 en el parque del Fòrum, en el que se alojan sus instalaciones destinadas a programas públicos: exposiciones, talleres, conferencias, mediateca, etc. La exposición permanente del mus

stops.name: Parc de Diagonal Mar
stops.en: Urban park created from redeveloping industrial land. It covers 14 hectares and includes seven areas like a children's play area, a lake with sculptures and a central plaza.

stops.name: Mercat del Born
stops.en: This market was the central market for Barcelona until 1973 and its closing marked the beginning of the neighborhood's decline before its current resurgence. While undergoing renovations, whole streets and homes that had been demolished by Phillipe V's orders were discovered and archaeologists who worked to transform the market in to a cultural centre and history museum. Entrance and street level

stops.name: International Convention Centre of Barcelona
stops.local: Centro de Convenciones Internacional de Barcelona

stops.name: Passeig del Born
stops.en: This avenue goes from the Santa Maria del Mar church to the Born market and is where the legendary jousting matches of the Middle Ages took place, as well as numerous fairs and marches. This is also where men were knighted. It is a really old street, very wide for the time. Don Quijote de la Mancha, the famous Cervantes character, had a contest in this place.

stops.name: Jardins de Miramar
stops.en: This is where you arrive by a harbour cable car. Marvelous place in the spring, full of roses and fountains. Entrance to the cactus garden is nearby. The Mirador Miramar offers splendid views over the city.

stops.name: Torre de les Aigües del Besòs
stops.local: Torre de las Aguas del Besós
stops.en: One of the most unusual landmarks in this otherwise ultra-modern area is this 19th-century (finished in 1882) brick water tower. Standing 62 metres tall, it is now overshadowed by neighbouring residential, office and hotel towers and easy to miss unless you know where to look for it.

stops.name: Museu Etnològic de Barcelona
stops.local: Museo Etnológico y de Culturas del Mundo
stops.en: This museum mainly exhibits exponents, which were imported by Catalan sailors as they explored the new world. Free on the first Sunday each month (11:00 to 15:00)

stops.name: University of Barcelona
stops.en: The university has many interesting buildings, libraries and courtyards.

stops.name: Plaça de Catalunya
stops.en: Connecting many of the major streets in the city, the Plaça is a central location and a hub of activity. It is a favourite meeting spot for locals and a transit hub for the tourist buses. There are many fountains, statues and gardens around the plaza, and a number of benches to just sit and take it all in.

stops.name: Museu Picasso
stops.en: Has a lot of art from his first period, before the cubism, but almost none of his most famous works. Pictures are described only in Spanish, but overview texts for each period are available in English. Luggage over 30x30cm needs to be left at the checkroom and there's no liability for lost valuables.

stops.name: FC Barcelona Museum
stops.en: Museum dedicated to the FC Barcelona. It occupies 3,500 m² and attracts 1.2 million visitors a year, ranking it second to the Museu Picasso, which attracts 1.3 million visitors, as the most visited museum in the city of Barcelona. All of the Barcas trophies and jerseys of many famous players of the team are exhibited. The museum can be visited by booking the Camp Nou Experience package, which incl

stops.name: Barcelona Zoo
stops.en: This zoo was famous for its albino gorilla Snowflake prior to his death. Today this zoo still has many other features including a science museum inside the zoo.

stops.name: Plaça d'Espanya
stops.en: Placa d'Espanya was created for the 1929 World Exhibition, on a site once used for public hangings. The fountain in the center of the square is a great attraction and plays music during the summer. Plaça Espanya is located at the base of Montjuic hill.

stops.name: Royal Square
stops.en: This square is famous for the nightlife and the uniform architecture, and features fountains and palm trees. It was built during the 19th century on the site of a monastery, after the Mendizábal law expelled the monks. After some years Antoni Gaudí designed the streetlights which are still there. It has lots of activity during the day, thanks to the many terraces of the bars and restaurants.

stops.name: plaça del Rei
stops.en: This square has two important buildings, the Santa Àgata church, where the kings from the Aragon crown had baptism. Is possible to visit it. The other building has the Saló del Tinell, one of the best civil Gothic architecture examples. Is the place where the royal receptions where held, so is very wide with a wooden ceiling hold by the typical Catalan Gothic arches. It has also a tower from which

stops.name: Port Vell de Barcelona
stops.en: The harbor was closed to the public until the 80s and received a complete makeover before the Olympics in 1992. Some old buildings related to the harbor still exist, such as the Tinglado near the Barceloneta quarter that is now a history museum. There are two main parts in the harbor: the Moll de la Fusta, which are the decks that touch the city, and the Maremagnum, a newly created amusement centr

stops.name: Port Olímpic
stops.en: It has a large number of restaurants, bars and other establishments. In this wide offer you can find also the Barcelona Casino.

stops.name: CaixaForum Barcelona
stops.en: Arts & cultural centre.

stops.name: Plaça de Sant Felip Neri
stops.en: One of the most romantic squares in Barcelona, it hides a dark history in that it was built over the city's old cemetery. Barcelona's most famous architect, Antonio Gaudi, was on his way to visit the church there when he was run over and killed in 1928. There is a baroque church (Sant Felip Neri), a 14th-century palace and a fountain in the middle. To arrive, take the narrow street next to the cat

stops.name: Synagogue Shlomo ben Adret
stops.en: They open during the morning. It is the re-discovered synagogue from the Jewish quarter, called call. This building, not very spectacular, is important since it has been here since the Roman era, and stayed as a synagogue until the Jewish exodus in the 15th century. The guide explains all the facts from the place in several languages.

stops.name: Museum of the History of Catalonia
stops.en: A must in order to understand the troubled and sad history of the Catalans.

stops.name: Design Museum of Barcelona
stops.en: Much to the dismay of Mickey Mouse aficionados, Disseny is Catalan for "design", not "Disney". The "Disseny Hub" houses the amalgamated museums focusing on applied arts and design, including Museu de les Arts Decoratives, Museu de Ceràmica, Museu Tèxtil i d'Indumentària and Gabinet de les Arts Gràfiques. The new building has an intricate, multi-level structure, with the protruding tower overhangin

stops.name: Centre d'Art Santa Mònica
stops.en: A contemporary art venue, showing solo exhibitions by national and international artists. Lots of other activities.

stops.name: Joan Antoni Samaranch Olympic and Sport Museum
stops.local: Museo Olímpico y del Deporte Juan Antonio Samaranch
stops.en: The museum displays high-performance sport competitions, recreational sports, sports in general and sports for disabled people. It shows how sport can promote values, educate, innovate and renew. The museum has a sport idols space with outstanding players.

stops.name: Erotic Museum Barcelona
stops.local: Museo de la Erótica de Barcelona
stops.en: Museum dedicated to erotic and sensual works. A huge tourist trap. The tour is not worth it, unless you wish to see old paintings of the Kama Sutra. The only interest is the huge phallus in the hallway, which makes for funny pictures.

stops.name: Plaça del Pi
stops.en: This square next to La Rambla is one of the prettiest parts of the quarter. It has a pine tree in the middle (Pi mines pine tree), the church of Santa Maria del Pi, which is a very pretty Gothic church with a huge rose window. Many concerts are held here. The Pi square and its twin square, called Sant Josep Oriol, have several bars and artisans, painters, musicians, who are there to sell their pro

stops.name: Museum of Mathematics of Catalonia
stops.en: The museum has limited opening hours but the park it is situated in is also interesting. Check website before going to the museum as it will eventually relocate to The Can Bagaria building.

stops.name: Carrer de Montcada
stops.en: This street has the biggest collection of Gothic houses in Barcelona. In amongst these houses is the Picasso Museum, which is definitely worth a visit. There are also smaller museums along the street, and many tapas restaurants though they may be more expensive on this street.

stops.name: Daughters of Charity of Saint Vincent de Paul
Museu d'Història de Barcelona
stops.en: Includes access to underground Roman ruins and a complex of historic buildings in the centre of the Barri Gòtic (Gothic Quarter), and is a reasonably good historical museum.

stops.name: Tibidabo Amusement Park
stops.en: Tibidabo is a popular attraction with stunning vistas, an historic amusement park, and the iconic Sagrat Cor church.

stops.name: Archaeology Museum of Catalonia
stops.en: Situated on the Montjuic, it exhibits archaeological findings from Catalunia from different periods. Under 16 and 65+ free. €3 for others. Special discounts for other groups.

stops.name: Museu de les Il·lusions
stops.en: A museum of more than 30 room-sized, hand-painted 3D murals built on forced perspective: visitors stand on marked spots and appear to hang from a dragon's jaw or teeter over a painted canyon. Photography is the point of the visit.

stops.name: Hotel Majestic
stops.en: Passeig de Gràcia 68. Enjoy city views from the rooftop. Just enter the elevator right from the lobby, and head up to the top floor.

stops.name: Barcelona Bus Turístic
stops.en: Operated by TMB with blue-and-red buses, it has three routes (map provided as you board), including a northbound and a southbound line that leave from opposite sides of the Plaça de Catalunya. Each takes 1–2 hours. The hop-on/hop-off format lets you get-off at any interesting stop, see what interests you, then get back on any later bus at that or any other stop. One approach is stay on for an enti

stops.name: Barcelona City Tour
stops.en: Operated by Moventis with red buses, it has two routes: the northbound green route that goes by the beaches and Barceloneta, as well as important landmarks like Plaça de Catalunya, Hospital de Sant Pau, and Parc Güell; as well as the southbound orange route that runs over the Montjuïc mountain and passes by the Sagrada Família and the Camp Nou football stadium.

stops.name: Carrer Petritxol
stops.en: This narrow street, that starts in the Plaça del Pi has a very special atmosphere. It is famous because of its chocolate shops, where you can drink a hot chocolate since the 18th century. It has also very important art galleries (Sala Parés, the place where Picasso made a dedicated exposition for the first time). You can enter for free and see, if you are lucky, nice expositions. The street is dec

stops.name: Park Güell, the main entrance
stops.en: Two Gaudi-style pavilions mark the entrance to the park and lead to the steps up to the Hipostila Room. In the middle of the steps is the dragon (or salamander) fountain that has become almost as much a symbol of Barcelona as the Sagrada Familia.

stops.name: Hipostila Room and Grand Plaza
stops.en: At the top of the stairs from the main entrance is the Hipostila Room with its 86 white columns supporting the plaza above. The ceiling has a number of colourful mosaics. Above the Hipostila Room is the main terrace, which was meant to be the main square of the development. It features a mosaic-tiled wall in the shape of an undulating sea serpent and provides excellent views of Barcelona.

stops.name: Turo de les tres creus
stops.en: This is the highest point of the park and where Gaudi wanted to build a chapel. After the development failed, Gaudi built a monolith with three crosses like Calvary instead. Be sure to take in the panoramic views of Barcelona.

stops.name: Basílica de la Sagrada Familia
stops.lc: Esta catedral es aclamada como la obra maestra de Antoni Gaudí y su construcción comenzó en 1882 según los diseños neogóticos de Francisco de Paula del Villar. Solo un año después de que comenzara la construcción, Gaudí se hizo cargo, adoptó un enfoque más modernista del proyecto que se convirtió en el trabajo de su vida. eats.name: Barcelona Eat Local Food Tours
eats.note: A family-owned business that showcases the best of Catalan gastronomy in off-the-beaten districts of Barcelona.

eats.name: Comer y no Bombas
eats.note: Shares free vegan food.

eats.name: El Glop

eats.name: Balordi
eats.note: Located near Plaça d’Espanya. Casual Italian street-food spot specialising in panini and handmade meatballs. Expect bold flavours and quick counter service, with a few sidewalk benches for eating in.

eats.name: Conesa Entrepans
eats.note: Cheap and very good sandwiches. Always with a lot of people. They have some tables inside. They close quite early at night (by Spanish standards).

eats.name: Travellers Nest Bar
eats.note: They serve meals, a full English breakfast and 8oz Irish rump steaks all day with ingredients imported from the UK.

eats.name: Maoz Vegetarian
eats.note: Offers excellent vegan falafel (including unlimited salad) for around €4. There are several around Barcelona including one on 95, La Rambla, about 10 minutes walk from Pl Catalunya.

eats.name: Mercado de La Boqueria

eats.name: Fres Co

eats.name: Bo de B
eats.note: Excellent sandwiches made with freshly chopped/cooked/baked ingredients on fantastic baguette (chicken with avocado sauce is recommended), plates, omelettes and salads for reasonable prices (between €

eats.name: BioCenter
eats.note: It offers tasty vegetarian and vegan food.

eats.name: La Bombeta
eats.note: Good tapas and more substantial dishes. A great alternative to the tourist traps along the waterfront. Very friendly.

eats.name: Vegetalia Gòtic

eats.name: Agua
eats.note: Creative cooking combining Catalonian traditions with Italian cuisine. The terrace outside showcases some great views of Barceloneta.

eats.name: Bar Bitácora
eats.note: The bar serves consistently good tapas - patas bravas, platos del dias - for fair price. In the evening many come for a drink.

eats.name: Cal Pep

eats.name: Los Caracoles

eats.name: Bar Pinotxo
eats.note: The best Catalan dishes. No reservations. Always full, don't be surprised if you aren't able to sit.

eats.name: Restaurante La Boqueria
eats.note: An emblematic restaurant in the centre of Barcelona to enjoy the city's local cuisine. Approximately €20 per person to eat dishes like Paella or Tapas.

eats.name: Restaurante Italiano Rossini
eats.note: Authentic Italian food in Plaza Real. Homemade pizzas, fresh pasta, Mediterranean tapas, meat and fish. Live piano music every day from 20:00.

eats.name: My Way Lounge Restaurant
eats.note: Gourmet Mediterranean cuisine near Plaza Real. Elegant decoration inspired by Art Deco, with paintings by Tamara de Lempicka. It's also a cocktail bar.

eats.name: The Clubhouse Laietana & Nikki's

eats.name: Can Culleretes

eats.name: La Dolca Herminia
eats.note: Same chain as Les Quinze Nits. No reservation accepted. Bit old-style and dark interior, judging by web site.

eats.name: Els Quatre Gats

eats.name: Elx Restaurant
eats.note: Valencian paella and Meditterian dishes. One of the few places available for tourists where paella is genuine enough.

eats.name: Café Silenus
eats.note: Also has excellent lunch offers. A design restaurant just in front of the MACBA. Mediterranean and Japanese cuisine.

eats.name: Al Passatore
eats.note: Pasta, pizza and risotto in very generous portions for moderate prices. No-frills dishes, but wide choice. Simple interior. Bread should be asked for explicitly. For dinner, reservation essential

eats.name: Betawi
eats.note: a really tasty Indonesian restaurant. Portions aren't huge (average) but they know how to cook meat and fish to perfection

eats.name: Shunka
eats.note: One of the most appreciated Japanese restaurants in town. Prior reservation is strongly advised.

eats.name: Cafe de L'Opera
eats.note: A marvellous place to have a breakfast with fine strong coffee. As the owner insists on coffee and desserts, they are the core competence. The inside features 1920s decor.

eats.name: Bestial
eats.note: Fabulous lunch specials to be enjoyed on their great beach terrace on warm sunny days. Dinner tends to be quite expensive, thus lunch is the value for money option.

eats.name: L'Antic Teatre

eats.name: Escriba
eats.note: Very old and beautiful confectionery.

eats.name: Catwalk
eats.note: One of the most popular nightclubs in the city, with the peak time around 02:00. They offer 2 floors with R&B and hip-hop styles mixed with House or Techno. A lot of teenagers go here.

eats.name: Comerç 24
eats.note: A fashion tapas bar. Very creative, very good.

eats.name: Danzantoria
eats.note: House music fans come here for the pumping beats and funky decor. Offers two floors of dancing, and a terrace to chill out on between dances.

eats.name: La Fianna
eats.note: One of the busiest bars in the neighborhood with a funky decor and a large selection of spirits. They also have a great dinner menu with an international selection.

eats.name: Le Kashbar
eats.note: With a Moroccan decor, Le Kashbar is the perfect spot to chill out on cushions and take in the ambient music.

eats.name: Opium
eats.note: Great club. Great music. Dance floor, lounge area, and outside bar.

eats.name: Cafè Milans
eats.note: Probably one of the most dynamic bars of the Gothic Area. DJ sessions, live exhibitions, art, and cocktails.

eats.name: RiBborn

eats.name: Shoko
eats.note: Designed by a Feng Shui expert, Shoko serves you good karma all night. Depending on the night, the dj usually spins House or Hip Hop tunes.

eats.name: Club Sauvage

eats.name: Irish Pub Temple Bar
eats.note: An Irish pub near Las Ramblas. A space where you can enjoy the best national and international beers, smash burgers, while you watch live games from our big screens.

eats.name: vegan Cat Bar
eats.note: Well chosen selection of craft beers with good selection of tasty vegan burgers and other dishes. (no fake meat)

eats.name: Black Lab Brewhouse & Kitchen
eats.note: Closed September 2025. Entry to be removed

eats.name: Ølgod Brewpub
eats.note: Craft ale mainly brewed on site.

eats.name: Restaurant Macrobiòtic Zen
eats.note: Vegan restaurant.

eats.name: Vegan Mount
eats.note: Vegan cafe

eats.name: La Flauta

eats.name: Le P'ty Mon

eats.name: El Ùltimo Agave
eats.note: Authentic Mexican restaurant.

eats.name: Vinitus
eats.note: Tapas and seafood

eats.name: Moo
eats.note: Renowned Catalan chef Joan Roca serves up tasty treats such as sea bass with lemongrass or a delicious suckling pig.

eats.name: Bracafe
eats.note: Nice cosy cafe to sit and lounge over a cup of proper coffee.

eats.name: Fàbrica Moritz Barcelona
eats.note: 'Moritz Epidor' absolutely should be tasted. Brewery tours available.

eats.name: Arena Xperience
eats.note: 3-story disco club.

eats.name: BIERCaB
eats.note: International craft beers a snacks

eats.name: Maresme Brewery Taproom
eats.note: Good choice of craft beers. Food available except Monday

eats.name: Frankfurt's Casa Valles
eats.note: Sells hamburgers and hot dogs at cheap prices, hence very popular for locals and young crowd in the evenings.

eats.name: La Caravana
eats.note: A Syrian restaurant

eats.name: Veg World - India
eats.note: A restaurant that serves only vegetarian food - mainly Indian dishes. This may be the only place in Barcelona where you can get Masala Dosa. Beware that the size of the dishes is not that big.

eats.name: Can Xurrades
eats.note: Probably one of the best Catalan restaurants in the neighbourhood, although their selection of other Spanish food is quite good. Particularly excels at meat dishes, cooked in traditional Catalan style

eats.name: Karakala
eats.note: The Lebanese restaurant has impeccable and friendly service. It serves authentic Lebanese food.

eats.name: Kibuka
eats.note: The Japanese sushi bar serves in convivial atmosphere different sushi plates, Japanese beer, sake, cocktails and wines too.

eats.name: La Rosa del Desierto
eats.note: The Moroccan food restaurant in Barcelona offering quality and generous portions, with a quite special decoration.

eats.name: Sol i Lluna
eats.note: This cosy restaurant serves good Mediterranean cuisine.

eats.name: Taverna El Glop

eats.name: Alkimia
eats.note: One of Barcelona's most highly regarded restaurants, run by acclaimed restaurateur Jordi Vilà. With a minimalist white interior that directs the attention to the inventive and indulgent foods on offer

eats.name: Botafumeiro
eats.note: Next door to La Taberna Del Cura, Botafumeiro specializes in seafood, while La Taberna handles the meats. High quality food with a price tag to match.

eats.name: D.O. vins i platillos
eats.note: The wine bar offers exquisite tapas and many local wine choices.

eats.name: Bobby Gin S.L.

eats.name: El Dorado

eats.name: La Cervesera Artesana
eats.note: Barcelona's first brew-pub still going strong. Tasty snacks to go with the beer.

eats.name: Koska Taverna
eats.note: The tapas bar has great drink choices and serves original non traditional food.

eats.name: Quimet & Quimet
eats.note: Lively little bar that serves excellent sandwiches and has a good selection of wines.

eats.name: La tasqueta de Blai
eats.note: The tapas bar is very popular and hence always packed. It offers interesting varieties including sweet dessert ones.

eats.name: Celler Cal Marino
eats.note: Wine bar with lots of local choices plus a great selection of cheeses. They have great suggestions according to personal taste.

eats.name: Gran Bodega Saltó
eats.note: Bar that seems out of the eighties. It is very popular and plays regular concerts.

eats.name: Maumau
eats.note: A chilled out lounge bar with groovy tunes that uses its space to host short film nights, installations and concerts. Their webpage is worth a look for upcoming events and shows in Barcelona.

eats.name: Sala Apolo
eats.note: It is one of the best clubs in town, and the place to be on Monday nights. Concerts every weekend and also during the week.

eats.name: Abirradero
eats.note: Brew pub in the Poble Sec area. A range of dishes to go with the beer.

eats.name: Vegan Food Heaven
eats.note: Bright & airy vegan fusion restaurant. on-line table reservation.

eats.name: L’Ovella Negra (The Black Sheep)

eats.name: La Riera
eats.note: Vegetarian restaurant with varied menu that uses seasonal ingredients from local markets.

eats.name: Can Punyetes
eats.note: A very traditional Catalan restaurant favored by locals. Menu in Catalan, but it's worth the risk, the food is delicious.

eats.name: Flash-Flash

eats.note: One of the most promising cuisines in Barcelona with excellent wine service.

eats.name: La Esquinica
eats.note: One of the best known tapas restaurants in Barcelona, there's usually a long queue outside.

eats.note: Cachitos Diagonal is a tapas restaurant on a cool, avant-garde stile. Bright and spacious, with large blackboards and ivy climbing on the walls, creates a warm, chic and stylish atmosphere.

eats.name: Cervecería Catalana
eats.note: En este animado sitio se sirven tapas tradicionales, montaditos y postres con asientos en la barra y mesas en la acera a la sombra. De la misma familia que el Ciudad Condal.

eats.name: Casa Lolea
eats.note: Espacio industrial decorado con lunares coloridos en donde se sirven tapas, montaditos y sangría.

eats.name: Ciutat Comtal
eats.note: Goza de una situación privilegiada y, aunque los precios no son baratos, está siempre abarrotado, cosa que habla a favor de la calidad de su oferta. De la misma familia que la Cervecería Catalana.

eats.name: Restaurante Agua
eats.note: Cocina creativa que combina las tradiciones catalanas con la cocina italiana. La terraza exterior muestra unas vistas geniales de la Barceloneta.

eats.name: Núria
eats.note: Restaurante de época que sirve tapas, carnes, pescados, paellas, pizzas y mojitos desde los años 20.

eats.name: Viana Restaurant

eats.note: Comedor pequeño y tranquilo para comer platos gallegos clásicos con un toque moderno. Precio medio-alto.

eats.note: Restaurante de carnes con recetas argentinas y carnes del mundo y pastas amasadas a mano en elegante local con columnas de ladrillo visto y lámparas de diseño.
